rules.title: California statewide rent cap (Tenant Protection Act, Civ. Code § 1947.12)
rules.requirement: An owner may not raise the gross rental rate over any 12-month period by more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, measured from the lowest gross rental rate charged in the prior 12 months. No more than two increments are allowed in 12 months for the same tenant, and notice must be given under Civ. Code § 827.
rules.key_value: 5% + CPI change, max 10% (whichever is lower), in any 12-month period; max two increments per 12 months
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential real property (any dwelling or unit intended for human habitation, including units in mobilehome parks). Does not apply to housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome). A new tenancy in which no prior tenant remains in lawful possession may be set at an initial rent not subject to the cap. Does not apply to a homeowner of a mobilehome.
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; dormitories of higher education or K-12 schools; housing under local rent/price control that limits annual increases to less than the state cap; housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (not mobilehomes); separately alienable property (e.g. single-family homes/condos) if the owner is not a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member (or mobilehome park management) and the tenant received the required written exemption notice; duplexes where the owner occupies one unit as principal residence (neither unit an ADU/JADU).
rules.interaction: Does not apply where a public entity's valid local rent or price control (consistent with Civ. Code ch. 2.7, § 1954.50 et seq.) restricts annual increases to less than the state cap. The section does not expand or limit local authority to adopt rent controls consistent with ch. 2.7 and does not authorize local limits not otherwise permissible under that chapter.
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower

rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: It is unlawful, and a violation of the NJ Antitrust Act, for a rental property owner to pay for or subscribe to a coordinator's services, for a coordinator to facilitate agreements restricting competition, for any person to perform a coordinating function, or for two or more persons to engage in or facilitate parallel pricing coordination. A coordinating function includes using nonpublic data from two or more owners in an algorithm to set or recommend rents, material lease terms or occupancy levels.
rules.key_value: Ban on algorithmic coordination of rents, material lease terms and occupancy levels; enforced as an NJ Antitrust Act violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any rental property owner (a person owning, directly or indirectly, one or more rental residential dwelling units) and to any coordinator operating algorithmic revenue management software or an algorithmic device. A residential dwelling unit is a house, apartment, accessory unit or other unit intended as a primary residence in the State.
rules.exemptions: Residential dwelling units exclude inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities. Not a coordinating function: research, statistical analysis or testing that does not feed into pricing; rent estimates made available to the public at no cost; real estate brokerage databases available on equal terms that do not set or recommend rents or collect competitively sensitive information; and government entities setting or limiting rents through affordability controls. Algorithmic device excludes certain human-analysis spreadsheets without AI and databases that only use an algorithm to query unprocessed data.
rules.interaction: Supplements the New Jersey Antitrust Act (P.L.1970, c.73) and does not authorize conduct already unlawful under other law. Section 6(b) bars municipalities from enacting ordinances that conflict with the act, except ordinances explicitly authorized or required by other law. Enforcement uses Antitrust Act sections 6 through 17, and the Attorney General must set up a complaint portal and may adopt rules.
rules.quoted_span: shall be unlawful and a violation of the “New Jersey Antitrust Act,” P.L.1970,

rules.title: Limitation on amount of security deposit (N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2)
rules.requirement: An owner or lessee may not require a security deposit of more than 1.5 times one month's rent for residential dwelling property. Any additional security collected from a tenant in a year may not exceed 10 percent of the current security deposit.
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent maximum; additional annual security max 10% of current deposit
rules.coverage_conditions: Real property used for dwelling purposes; applies to owners or lessees collecting security from a tenant.
rules.interaction: State-wide rule; the document does not discuss municipal interaction.
rules.quoted_span: An owner or lessee may not require more than a sum equal to 1 1/2 times 1 month's rental according to the terms of contract, lease, or agreement as a security for the use or rental of real property used for dwelling purposes.
